Chapter 6: Praying Through Seasons of Change and Hardship
Life has a way of surprising us, doesn’t it? Every marriage goes through seasons of change—some you’re ready for, others that just show up out of nowhere. Maybe it’s the joy and upheaval of welcoming a new baby, the worry that comes with illness, a big career move, or the sorrow of loss. Each moment brings its own mix of challenges, but also opportunities to grow.
In these shifting times, prayer can feel like an anchor—something steady to hold onto when everything else seems up in the air.
Here’s something to pay attention to: change, even when it’s uncomfortable, is just a natural part of any long-term relationship. Instead of resisting or fearing what’s new, couples can choose to meet these seasons with open hearts and a little bit of faith.
Prayer isn’t just a routine—it’s a way to sort through your feelings, ask for guidance, and find hope, even when you don’t have all the answers.
So, how do you pray through times of change? Here’s a simple, gentle framework to try:
First, ask for resilience and adaptability. Life will bring surprises, and having the strength to adjust makes all the difference.
Next, pray for unity and understanding, especially when stress tries to push you apart.
When you’re in pain or feeling let down, seek comfort and strength.
And finally, invite gratitude—thankfulness for the lessons and growth that come with change.
Let’s make it real with a couple of examples. Picture a couple welcoming their first child. It’s incredibly exciting, but it’s also exhausting and sometimes overwhelming. Praying together for patience, energy, and the ability to support each other can make those sleepless nights just a little bit easier to handle.
Or think about facing a job loss or a health scare. In those moments, prayer can bring a sense of peace and direction, even if the path forward isn’t totally clear yet.
It’s easy to feel like hardship means you’ve failed somehow, but that’s just not true. Every couple will face storms—what matters most is how you weather them together. Prayer doesn’t magically make the hard things disappear, but it does change how you go through them. It helps shift your focus from fear to trust, and from feeling alone to standing together.
When couples lean into prayer during seasons of change, they don’t just get through it—they grow stronger and closer. They find out they’re more resilient than they ever imagined, and they discover new strengths in themselves and in each other.
So, as you move through whatever changes come your way, remember—you’re not alone. With prayer, you can find hope, unity, and even gratitude, no matter what season you’re in.
